thread:
Ellie: hey all — first week here, trying to build the runtime from source on WSL2. nvcc --version shows 12.2, CUDA toolkit is /usr/local/cuda, but configure && make errors out with undefined refs to cublasLt and a bunch of libcuda symbols. ldd on the binary says: libcuda.so.1 => not found. any quick checklist?

Omar: welcome! :tada: first check: can you run nvidia-smi inside WSL? also run `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` to see where linker thinks libcuda lives. WSL sometimes puts driver libs in /usr/lib/wsl/ or /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/.

Ellie: thanks — nvidia-smi fails with "command not found" inside WSL. on Windows the GPU works. I did install the CUDA toolkit in the distro but maybe I missed the driver piece?

Kevin: in WSL you still need the Windows NVIDIA driver with WSL support. On Win side install the WSL-compatible driver (the one from NVIDIA for Windows). After that, restart WSL and check `nvidia-smi` in the distro. If `nvidia-smi` appears, `libcuda` should be exposed.

Ellie: ok installed the WSL driver and restarted. nvidia-smi now shows output. `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` still empty though. ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so shows "not found" for libcuda.so.1

Omar: that's expected — the driver provides libcuda in a system path, not in /usr/local/cuda by default. You can either create a symlink into CUDA lib64 or update ld.so config. Try:
```
sudo ln -s $(ldconfig -p | grep libcuda.so.1 | awk '{print $NF}') /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so.1
sudo ldconfig
ldconfig -p | grep libcuda
```
If ldconfig -p didn't list libcuda earlier, try `find / -name libcuda.so* 2>/dev/null` to locate it.

Ellie: ldconfig -p still empty before the driver restart, but find returned `/usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so.1`. I did the ln -s to /usr/local/cuda/lib64 and ran sudo ldconfig. build now gets past the cublasLt refs but hits a linker complaint: undefined reference to cuGetProcAddress.

Kevin: cuGetProcAddress is in newer drivers / CUDA versions. Make sure the linker is seeing the right libcuda (the symlink points to the file you found). Also check your link order: -lcuda should come before any libraries that reference it. Try `gcc -Wl,-verbose` or inspect the final link line from the build logs.

Rosie: also check that you're not mixing a system-installed libcuda with a toolkit from a different ABI. `readelf -s /usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so.1 | grep cuGetProcAddress` can confirm symbol presence. If symbol missing, you probably need a newer driver.

Ellie: ran readelf, cuGetProcAddress is present. build still fails with "undefined reference" at link time though. copying the raw link line here: `g++ ... -L/usr/local/cuda/lib64 -lcudart -lcublas -lcuda -Wl,--start-group ... -Wl,--end-group`

Omar: put -lcuda at the end or inside the group after other libs that depend on it — the order matters. Example: `... -Wl,--start-group -lcublas -lcudart -lcuda -Wl,--end-group`. Also ensure `-Wl,-rpath,/usr/local/cuda/lib64` or LD_LIBRARY_PATH points to the symlink during runtime.

Ellie: reordering libs fixed the undefined refs, thanks! one last weird thing: when I run unit tests in docker they can't access /dev/nvidia0: permission denied. any tips for running GPU containers from WSL?

Rosie: use the `--gpus=all` flag or configure docker's default runtime with nvidia. On WSL, install `nvidia-container-toolkit` in the distro and start docker with GPU support. Also ensure your user is in the docker group and /dev/nvidia* have proper permissions: `ls -l /dev/nvidia*`.

Ellie: I tried `--gpus all` and it still errors inside the container: "failed to start container: error gathering device information: no such file or directory". looks like /dev/nvidiactl not present inside container.

Kevin: that usually means docker daemon isn't configured to expose the devices. Check `/etc/docker/daemon.json` for the nvidia runtime config and restart docker. On WSL you may also need to enable integration in Docker Desktop and check "Expose daemon on tcp://localhost" is off.

devops-bot: quick reminder: don't run docker with sudo in CI images; add user to docker group and use the runner token.

Ellie: turning on Docker Desktop WSL integration + installing nvidia-container-toolkit inside distro fixed it. containers see /dev/nvidiactl now. build+tests green locally. huge thanks everyone. :pray:

Omar: awesome — welcome aboard. If you want, push a short onboarding note to the eng-runtime README about the WSL quirks (where we symlink libcuda, docker toolkit), saved me time last month.

Ellie: will do and link the exact commands I used. thanks again!
